title: Generation of TCRα-transduced T cells for adoptive transfer therapy of salmonellosis in mice
protocol: Thaw one vial of cryopreserved HEK293T cells in a 37°C water bath.
Seed 1.0 × 10^6 HEK293T cells per T25 flask in 5 mL DMEM supplemented with 4.5 g/L glucose and 10% fetal bovine serum.
Grow the seeded cells in an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 to achieve 60-80% confluence.
In a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, mix 6 μg of pCL-Eco plasmid and 6 μg of MigR1-PGK-TCRa-SM with sterile ddH2O to a final volume of 225 μL.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Add 25 μL of 2 M CaCl₂ by pipetting.
Mix gently but thoroughly after each addition of CaCl₂.
Add 250 μL of 2× HBS drop-wise while agitating gently.
Incubate the resulting mixture for 5 min at 20–22°C.
Prepare a similar transfection mix with pCL-Eco and MigR1-PGK-GFP.
Remove growth medium from T25 flasks.
Add 5 mL of fresh DMEM to HEK293T cells.
Place the flask in a horizontal position to ensure all cells are covered by the medium.
Add one transfection mix drop-wise to an individual HEK293T flask.
Gently agitate the medium to uniformly distribute the transfection mix.
Place HEK293T flasks into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Check the transfection efficiency in the HEK293T flask using a fluorescent microscope after 24 hours.
Remove the growth medium containing plasmids from T25 flasks.
Add 5 mL of fresh DMEM to the HEK293T flasks.
Place HEK293T flasks into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for another 24 hours.
Collect the growth medium from HEK293T flasks in individual 15 mL centrifuge tubes after 48 hours.
Centrifuge the collected medium at 200 × g for 5 minutes to precipitate any residual cells.
Filter the supernatant containing viral particles into new sterile 15 mL tubes to obtain 5 mL of virus batch 1.
Add 5 mL of fresh DMEM to HEK293T flasks.
Place HEK293T flasks into an incubator for another 24 hours after adding fresh medium.
Collect the growth medium from HEK293T flasks in individual 15 mL centrifuge tubes after 72 hours.
Centrifuge the collected medium at 200 × g for 5 minutes to precipitate any residual cells.
Filter the supernatant containing viral particles into new sterile 15 mL tubes to obtain 5 mL of virus batch 2.
Handle HEK293T cells with care to avoid rough medium flow or agitation.
Collect supernatants with viral particles at 48 and 72 hours post-transfection.
Freeze collected supernatants at -70°C for storage.
Wrap the tube cap with parafilm before freezing.
Aliquot virus batch 1 and virus batch 2 into 4 mL volumes.
Use one aliquot (4 mL) of each batch to transduce up to 18.0 × 10^6 activated mouse T cells.
Store virus aliquots at -70°C, avoiding repeated freeze/thaw cycles.
Isolate spleen and mesenteric, inguinal, and axillary lymph nodes from a euthanized mouse.
Place the organs in Potter homogenizers containing 3 mL of 1× PBS.
Gently squeeze cells from organ stroma using a conical pestle.
Filter the resulting cell suspensions through a nylon filter (50 μm) to remove cell debris into individual 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the cell suspensions at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the cell pellets.
Resuspend LNs cell pellet in 3 mL of 1× PBS.
Resuspend splenocytes pellet in 1× RBC Lysis Buffer (Invitrogen).
Follow the manufacturer’s instructions to remove erythrocytes.
After erythrocyte lysis, resuspend the splenocyte pellet in 3 mL of 1× PBS.
Combine resulting suspensions of LNs cells and splenocytes into one 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the combined cell pellets.
Resuspend cells in 15 mL RPMI medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 5×10−5 M 2-mercaptoethanol, 2 mM L-glutamine, 20 mM HEPES, and 10 μg/mL Ciprofloxacin.
Homogenize the spleen and LNs in individual 40 mm Petri dishes in 3 mL 1× PBS using a 2 mL syringe plunger.
Resuspend the cell suspension by pipetting with a 1 mL pipette (5–10 times).
Transfer the resulting cell suspension into a 15 mL centrifuge tube through a nylon filter.
Transfer the entire cell suspension into a T75 flask.
Add 45 μL ConA to the final concentration of 3.0 μg/mL.
Add 15 μL IL-2 to the final concentration of 10.0 U/mL.
Gently agitate the flask to mix and uniformly disturb ConA and IL-2.
Place the flask into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Collect cells from the T75 flask into a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube 24 hours post-activation of mouse T cells.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 3 mL complete RPMI medium.
Count cells in Goryaev chamber or hemocytometer after trypan blue-eosin staining.
Resuspend cells in complete RPMI medium to a final concentration of 3.0 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer 1 mL of cell suspension containing 3.0 × 10^6 activated T cells into one well of a 6-well plate.
Generate control non-transduced T cells by transferring 3.0 × 10^6 activated T cells into a T75 flask in 10 mL complete RPMI medium.
Add 15 μL ConA to the final concentration of 1.5 μg/mL and 10 μL IL-2 to the final concentration of 10.0 U/mL, mix gently.
Place the flask into an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 48 hours.
Add 5 mL complete RPMI medium, 7.5 μL ConA to the final concentration of 1.5 μg/mL and 5 μL IL-2 to the final concentration of 10.0 U/mL, mix gently.
Place the flask back into the incubator for 3 days.
Use these non-transduced activated T cells as the negative control for in vivo adoptive transfer experiments.
Add 4 mL of virus batch 1 TCRα-SM or GFP and 3 mL of complete RPMI medium to a final volume of 8 mL per well.
Thaw one aliquot of virus batch 1 and warm up on a water bath at 37°C before adding to activated T cells.
Add 8 μL IL-2 (10,000 U/mL) to each well to achieve a final concentration of 10.0 U/mL.
Add 6.4 μL polybrene (10.0 mg/mL) to each well to reach a final concentration of 8.0 μg/mL.
Mix gently but thoroughly by pipetting with a 1 mL pipette (2-3 times).
Wrap the plate lid with parafilm and spinoculate plates at 2,000 × g for 2 h at 22°C.
Resuspend cells in each well using a 5 mL pipette (5–10 times) to avoid cell aggregation.
Check through each well under a light microscope to ensure cells are well resuspended.
Place the plate into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 16-20 h.
Collect all cells from each well in individual 15 mL sterile centrifuge tubes using a 5 mL pipette.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 4 mL complete RPMI medium.
Seed all cells back into the corresponding well of the plate.
Add 4 mL of virus batch 2 TCRα-SM or GFP to each well to achieve a final volume of 8 mL per well.
Thaw one aliquot of virus batch 2 and warm up on a water bath at 37°C before adding to a well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2–4 hours.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL complete RPMI medium.
Add 22.5 μL ConA (1.0 mg/mL) to the cell suspension.
Add 15 μL IL-2 (10,000 U/mL) to the cell suspension.
Mix gently but thoroughly by pipetting with a 5 mL pipette (2–3 times).
Transfer all cell suspensions into individual T75 flasks.
Add 5 mL complete RPMI medium to each flask to reach a final volume of 15 mL.
Incubate the flasks at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Control cell growth daily to avoid overgrowth.
If required, add extra complete RPMMI medium supplemented with 1.5 μg/mL ConA and 10.0 U/mL IL-2.
Collect transduced T cells into individual 15 mL centrifuge tubes on ice.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Gently resuspend transduced T cells in 5 mL sterile 1× PBS.
Count cells in Goryaev chamber or hemocytometer after trypan blue-eosin staining.
Aliquot approximately 3.0 × 10^5 cells from each tube and transfer to round-bottom flow cytometry tubes.
Add 1 mL of 1× PBS and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant, gently resuspend cells in 100 μL of 1× PBS.
Add Fc block antibodies (0.1 μg per 10^5 cells), incubate cells for 10 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge tubes at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C, remove the supernatant.
Gently resuspend cells in 100 μL of 1× PBS.
Add anti-CD3 and anti-Vα fluorescent antibodies, incubate cells 30–40 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 1 mL 1× PBS to the cell mixture.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend cells in 500 μL 1× PBS.
Add 10 μL PI (10.0 μg/mL) to all tubes.
Set a gate on lymphocytes by SSC-A versus FSC-A parameters.
Gate singlet cells by FSC-H versus FSC-A parameters.
Gate live cells as Percp-Cy5.5 negative on Percp-Cy5.5_Log histogram.
Set a dotplot for CD3 versus Va2 for live singlet cells, then gate CD3+ cells.
Set Va2_Log histogram for CD3+ live singlet cells and gate Va2+ cells.
Set FITC_Log histogram for CD3+ live singlet cells and gate FITC+ cells as GFP+ cells.
Collect 105 cells from the lymphocyte gate to analyze transduction efficacy.
Set CD3 versus Va2 dotplot for non-transduced T cells and TCRα-SM1 transduced T cells.
Gate CD3+ cells in both populations.
Set Va2 histogram for CD3+ cells.
Gate Va2+ cells to evaluate percent of Va2+ T cells.
Subtract the percentage of Va2+ cells in the population of non-transduced T cells from the percentage of Va2+ cells in the transduced T cell population to calculate transduction efficacy.
Set FITC histogram for CD3+ live singlet cells in GFP-transduced T cells.
Gate FITC+ cells to evaluate transduction efficacy in GFP-transduced T cells.
Evaluate the therapeutic potential of transduced T cells by performing adoptive transfer on day 3 post-infection in mice infected with virulent Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.
Evaluate the prophylactic potential of transduced T cells by performing adoptive transfer 3 days prior to infection in mice.

Calculate the concentration of transduced T cells using the formula Ctransduced cells = Ctotal × Transduction coefficient, where Ctransduced cells is the concentration of transduced T cells (×10^6/mL), Ctotal is the total cell concentration in the tube (×10^6/mL) as counted previously, and Transduction coefficient is the transduction efficacy divided by 100.

Determine the concentration of TCRa-SM transduced T cells with a given example: If the total cell concentration in the corresponding tube is 5.0 × 10^6/mL and the transduction efficacy for TCRa-SM1 is 71.4%, then the Transduction coefficient would be 0.714.
Calculate the final concentration of TCRa-SM1 transduced T cells as 3.57 × 10^6/mL by multiplying the total cell concentration with the Transduction coefficient (5.0 × 0.714).
Mix 1.5 × 10^5 transduced TCRa-SM16 cells with 1.5 × 10^5 transduced TCRa-SM21 cells to a final volume of 200 μL per mouse for therapeutic adoptive transfer.
Mix 1.0 × 10^5 transduced TCRa-SM1, TCRa-SM14, and TCRa-SM20 each to a final volume of 200 μL per mouse for prophylactic adoptive transfer.
Do not exceed a total dose of 3.0 × 10^5 cells/mouse for transduced T cells to avoid toxic side-effects.
Never inject more than 3.0 × 10^5 cells/mouse to prevent cytokine storm and immunosuppression in vivo.
Aliquot non-transduced T cells to a final dose of 3.0 × 105/Transduction coefficient per mouse in 200 μL 1× PBS.
Mix 10.7 × 105 total TCRa-SM16 cells and 10.7 × 105 total TCRa-SM21 cells in 1.0 mL 1× PBS for therapeutic adoptive transfer to 5 mice.
Mix 7.1 × 105 total TCRa-SM1, TCRa-SM14, and TCRa-SM20 cells each in 1.0 mL 1× PBS for prophylactic adoptive transfer to 5 mice.
Ensure transduction efficacy is above 50% before use of TCRa-SM transduced T cells for adoptive transfer.
Thoroughly mix cell suspension before sampling an aliquot.
Transfer 200 μL of cell suspension into a mouse through the retro-orbital sinus using an insulin syringe.
Keep cell suspensions on ice throughout the adoptive transfer procedure.
Thaw one vial of cryopreserved S. enterica serovar Typhimurium strain IE 147 in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer bacterial cells into 5 mL LB broth and incubate in a thermostatic shaker at 185 rpm at 37°C for 18 hours.
Prepare 7 serial 10x dilutions of the bacterial culture in sterile PBS.
Seed 500 μL of bacterial cells from 10−6 and 10−7 dilutions onto individual Petri dishes with SS agar.
Incubate Petri dishes at 37°C for 12 hours.
Count colonies on each Petri dish to calculate the concentration of salmonella in LB broth (CFU/mL).
Aliquot 4–6 × 10^6 CFU of bacterial cells and dilute in sterile PBS to a final volume of 200 μL per mouse.
Determine LD50 for each specific experimental model when using different virulent strains and mice lines.
Infect mice per os with 200 μL suspension of bacterial cells using a syringe with a blunt 22G gavage needle.
Euthanize mice on day 7 post-infection.
Aseptically isolate the spleen.
Prepare homogenates from each spleen using the SilentCrusher M homogenizer in 1 mL sterile 1× PBS.
Dilute the resulted spleen homogenate by mixing 900 μL of PBS with 100 μL of cell suspension to create a 10× dilution.
Seed 500 μL of the diluted spleen homogenates onto individual Petri dishes with SS agar.
Incubate Petri dishes at 37°C for 18–24 hours.
Count the number of bacterial colonies on each Petri dish.
Calculate bacterial CFU per spleen.
